transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Recording id: ff-20251203-novus-lowbit-pilot-001
Attendees: Jordan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marco Li (Solutions Eng), Sam Ortega (Redwood CSM); Aisha Patel (Novus ML), Tom Reyes (Novus Head ML), Claire Dubois (Novus Security), Ben Ortiz (Novus SRE)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync on the low-bit (INT8/FP8) pilot. Reviewed quality regressions observed on the clinical summarization workload, walked through per-prompt deltas, discussed adjustments (bias correction, attention fallback), and next steps to narrow root causes. Agreed to rerun a 1k-case batch with new knobs and share a prioritized list of failing prompts. Also touched on deployment mode implications (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and compliance checklist items.

Topics:
- Perf deltas: throughput and median latency changes under INT8 vs FP8
- Quality deltas: top regressions and signal/noise analysis
- Tuning knobs: attention fallback, kv-cache persistence, bias-correction, prompt-sanitization
- Infra: dedicated capacity pricing, burst behavior, on-prem checklist for private
- Compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, data residency questions

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Miller: Alright everyone, thanks for hopping on. Short agenda: results walk through, tuning options, and next run. Priya, you want to lead on the perf/quality bits?
[00:18] Priya Shah: Yeah, for sure. I'll open the spreadsheet -- um the sheet is called lowbit-runs-v3, link shared in the chat. Quick context: we ran three variants, baseline fp16, int8 with per-channel quant, and fp8 prototype. We logged token-level deltas and end-to-end latency.
[00:37] Aisha Patel: Quick ask first—are the prompt sets identical across runs? We noticed a small jitter in tokenization earlier.
[00:45] Priya Shah: Good point. Yes we used the identical seed batch, but there was an extra cleanup step in the fp8 run that removed some trailing whitespace—could affect a couple short prompts. Noted.
[01:05] Marco Li: Also to call out, KV cache behavior changed slightly in int8 path on our runtime build 2.1.1, so prefix caching might miss some hits; that's likely a perf delta cause. We added a conservative patch last night to keep cache layout stable.
[01:28] Tom Reyes: When you say "perf delta" what's the ballpark? We need numbers to justify moving to dedicated GPUs.
[01:35] Priya Shah: Median token latency: baseline fp16 12.3 ms/token, FP8 10.7 ms/token (about -13%), INT8 8.9 ms/token (-28%), though tail latency increases on INT8 by ~15% in worst-case sequences. Throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) improved accordingly on INT8.
[01:57] Ben Ortiz: Tail latency bump is our concern; clinical routing needs 95th < 200ms. Are the worst-case prompts pathological or common?
[02:10] Priya Shah: We profiled top 20 regressions; about 14 of them are long-code-block or heavy-table formatting prompts which cause attention matrix shapes to flip. Those expose quantization sensitivity.
[02:32] Claire Dubois: On quality, what's the measured degrade? We need concrete metrics for our regulated pipeline.
[02:40] Priya Shah: We computed ROUGE-L and a custom clinical-entity F1. FP8 averages -1.8% ROUGE-L compared to fp16, INT8 average -4.5% ROUGE-L. For entity F1, FP8 -0.7 pts, INT8 -2.2 pts. But noise varies by prompt type.
[03:05] Aisha Patel: Hmm, for certain extraction prompts that's significant. Can you show an example?
[03:12] Priya Shah: Sure, slide 7 has a before/after. Example prompt id 2145: baseline extracts all medication entries, INT8 missed second-line dosage in 3/5 runs. We suspect small bias shifts in the final head.
[03:34] Jordan Miller: This is where bias-correction helps; we can apply a lightweight output-layer calibration using a small validation set to correct for systematic shifts. That usually recovers a chunk of the loss for token-sensitive tasks.
[03:49] Tom Reyes: Is that safe for clinical? We need traceability and reproducibility—can't be a black-box fix.
[03:57] Marco Li: Absolutely, we'll log the calibration weights, seed, and version. We can lock the calibration artifact to the model rollout and include it in the audit trail—works with your KMS for signing if needed.
[04:14] Claire Dubois: Speaking of audit, is there an established pattern for audit logs when running in Redwood Private? Do we get per-request provenance?
[04:22] Sam Ortega: Yes, Private includes per-request tracing, and we support sending logs to your SIEM. We can also enable immutable append-only logs and integrate with your KMS/HSM for signing. We'll follow up with the SOC2 docs.
[04:38] Aisha Patel: Back to regressions—are these reproducible deterministically? Or do we see intermittent flakiness?
[04:46] Priya Shah: Most are reproducible when using the same seeds and the exact tokenization. A few are flaky, likely due to beam search nondeterminism in quant builds. We have a deterministic decode toggle to reduce variance; it slows things slightly.
[05:03] Ben Ortiz: Could that toggle be acceptable in production? Slowing is a tradeoff. What delta?
[05:09] Priya Shah: Deterministic decode added around +6% median latency, but reduced variance and fixed about 60% of the flaky cases.
[05:21] Tom Reyes: We should prioritize: 1) fix deterministic flakiness, 2) bias-correction, 3) attention fallback for long tables. Agreed?
[05:29] Aisha Patel: Agreed. Also need to see the raw examples, not just metrics.
[05:37] Jordan Miller: We'll put the 50 highest-impact failing prompts in the shared folder. Aisha, can you flag which ones are must-fix vs acceptable degradation?
[05:46] Aisha Patel: Yes, will do. We'll mark them with severity tags.
[05:51] Priya Shah: For the attention fallback—it's a runtime knob to fall back to FP16 attention computation selectively on sequences detected as risky (tables, code). That keeps the rest of the tokens in INT8 fast path. It costs about +5% latency on sequences where it's triggered, but recovers quality.
[06:12] Tom Reyes: Sounds promising. Do you have heuristics for detection?
[06:18] Marco Li: Heuristics are length + token-type pattern, and we can also add a small classifier to predict "attention-risk" using a cheap embed. It's configurable.
[06:27] Claire Dubois: Any compliance implications of a hybrid path?
[06:31] Sam Ortega: Not really—it's a deterministic behavior controlled in config and audited. All config changes are logged.
[06:37] [07:00] Jordan Miller: Let's talk pricing and deployment. If we move to dedicated GPUs for INT8, what's the rough cost delta?
[07:08] Priya Shah: In our spreadsheet we have an estimated cost per million tokens. INT8 on dedicated gives about 42% reduction in $/token vs fp16 hosted due to better density. FP8 sits around 28% reduction but with less tail risk. I'll send the updated TCO with dedicated/reserved and burst assumptions.
[07:30] Tom Reyes: For compliance we are leaning Private; does Private support the quant runtime and the same performance characteristics?
[07:38] Marco Li: Private supports the same runtime, but on-prem hardware variance matters; we validate kernel support for INT8/FP8 on target GPUs. Some customers need specific CUDA/driver combos for FP8 paths. We'll share the compatibility matrix.
[07:56] Ben Ortiz: We run mixed GPU fleet; can Redwood Dedicated spillover to Private if reserved capacity is saturated?
[08:03] Jordan Miller: We can implement policy-based routing: preferred dedicated, fallback to hosted compatible model variant, and last to private if configured. But cross-account private spillover is non-trivial—needs network peering. We'll detail options.
[08:20] Aisha Patel: On the technical deep-dive front, we should schedule a separate session with your SREs to review kernel-level diffs and any ABI mismatches. Some of our infra folks saw a few CUDA warnings on the INT8 build.
[08:33] Priya Shah: Agreed. Marco and Ben, let's align on a time.
[08:38] Ben Ortiz: I can do Thurs morning PST next week.
[08:42] Jordan Miller: Noted.
[08:44] [09:30] Priya Shah: Quick note on quality measurement: we added significance testing per prompt; a lot of micro-deltas are within noise. We're focusing the alerting on statistically significant regressions and business-impacting entity drops.
[09:55] Tom Reyes: For the 50 failing prompts, can you annotate which ones are high business impact and which are edge cases?
[10:02] Priya Shah: Yes, we'll annotate with "impact: high/med/low" and the root-cause hypothesis column.
[10:10] Aisha Patel: Also include the fail rate distribution over runs so we can see flakiness.
[10:16] Priya Shah: Will do.
[10:20] Marco Li: On a runtime note: we think a pragmatic mid-term approach is to run FP8 in production with attention-fallback + a small calibration layer for sensitive outputs. INT8 is great for cost but we recommend a progressive rollout after the rerun and regression reduction.
[10:40] Tom Reyes: Makes sense. For our stakeholders, we need a short one-pager recommendation: quick exec summary, risks, and timeline.
[10:48] Jordan Miller: We'll draft that. Jordan action item: create recommendation doc with option A/B/C and TCO.
[10:56] Priya Shah: One more experimental knob: token-level bias smoothing — we apply a tiny temperature shift per head to stabilize numeric underflow in INT8; it helped on some entity extraction tests. Caveat: it's heuristic.
[11:12] Aisha Patel: Could that be considered a model change from a regulatory standpoint?
[11:18] Claire Dubois: Potentially. If it changes outputs materially we need approval. Keep it transparent in the changelog.
[11:26] Priya Shah: Understood. We'll surface the exact math and baseline tests.
[11:33] [12:00] Jordan Miller: Let's recap next steps — Priya will run 1k rerun with bias-correction, attention-fallback toggled off/on, deterministic decode on/off. Share raw deltas and annotated 50 prompts. Jordan will share TCO and the short recommendation doc. Sam will share SOC2 and audit integration notes. Customer to produce prompt flags and severity.
[12:22] Tom Reyes: Sounds good. Proposed timeline? We want decision input by Dec 15.
[12:27] Jordan Miller: We're targeting the rerun results and docs in hand by Dec 9, review Dec 10-11, decision window Dec 15.
[12:36] Ben Ortiz: Quick nit—there were some transcription errors in last week's notes: "K V cash" instead of KV cache; keep real names.
[12:44] Jordan Miller: Good catch, we'll clean up the meeting notes.
[12:50] [13:10] Priya Shah: One more thing: shared artifact links -- lowbit-runs-v3 (spreadsheet), failing-prompts/novus/top50.json, tco-deltas/v1. Links posted in the chat.
[13:24] Aisha Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll upload the severity tags today.
[13:30] Jordan Miller: Thanks team. Sam will follow up with SOC2 packet; we'll schedule infra deep-dive. Meeting adjourned.
